questions.stem: A job stops at its time limit with no plan, and MathOpt's best_objective_bound() returns inf. The service sends a pydantic model whose bound field is declared as a plain float. What happens?

options.text: The JSON says Infinity, and reading it back gives the float inf
options.says: Only json.dumps writes Infinity; pydantic writes null for an infinite float.

options.text: The JSON says null, and reading it back as a float raises an error
options.says: Right: pydantic wrote {"bound":null}, and reading it back failed with 'Input should be a valid number'.

options.text: The reply is a 500, since pydantic refuses to write an infinite float
options.says: Pydantic wrote the value without complaint, as null; nothing failed until the JSON was read back.

options.text: The JSON says 1.8e308, since pydantic caps an infinite float
options.says: No number is substituted; the run shows null.

origin.section: No Plan Means null, Never Infinity

questions.stem: Lesson 12.4.3's schema_rules.py builds results by hand. Which of these did PlanResult refuse?

options.text: optimal with a plan, npv 900, bound 950 and gap 0.06
options.says: Printed as accepted: the validator does not check that a proven plan's gap is 0.

options.text: time_limit with no plan, npv null, bound 1,000 and gap null
options.says: Printed as accepted: with no npv, no gap is expected, and a bound may stand alone.

options.text: time_limit with a plan, npv 900, bound null and gap 0.11
options.says: Right: a gap needs both npv and bound, so the validator refused it.

options.text: optimal with a plan, npv 900, bound 900 and gap 0.00
options.says: The consistent result, printed as accepted.

origin.section: Every Field Has One Meaning, and the Schema Refuses Results That Contradict Themselves

questions.stem: Lesson 12.4.3's planner_client.py draws the small portfolio's result with the 2029 budget cut to $7,000k. What did its summary show?

options.text: NPV $23,645k, and the year with $0k of headroom was 2029
options.says: 2029 kept $30k of headroom; 2030 was spent to the last thousand.

options.text: NPV $23,645k, and the year with $0k of headroom was 2031
NPV $24,260k, and the year with $0k of headroom was 2030
options.says: $24,260k is the uncut plan's NPV; the cut cost $615k.

options.text: NPV $23,645k, and the year with $0k of headroom was 2030
options.says: Right: the tool printed NPV $23,645k and 2030 at 8,610 of 8,610.

origin.section: A Planner Tool Declares Only What It Reads, and the Service Only Adds Fields
